messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert triggered: multiple 525 TLS handshake failures across API edge (us-west), grouped by Cloudflare edge IPs.
pagerduty: @maria oncall — high priority incident page.
maria oncall: I’m awake, looking. Seeing spike in 525 and CONNECT_TIMEouts in the logs.
alex infra: Confirming — our load balancers show healthy backend 200s, errors originate before reaching origin.
kia sre: This looks like Cloudflare edge -> origin TLS handshake failures. Any recent cert/key rotations?
maria oncall: No cert changes on our side in last 24h. I’m pulling Cloudflare connection logs now.
sam support: Customer reports: API calls failing intermittently, some 502/524 for public customers. Raised on support queue, tagging product.
tyler eng-runtime: Quick check: KV cache hits unaffected for successful requests, failed requests fail during TCP/TLS handshake stage. Sample curl shows:
```
curl -Iv https://api.redwood.dev/ -H 'Host: api.redwood.dev'
* About to connect() to 104.16.101.2 port 443
*   Trying 104.16.101.2... connected.
* TLS handshake failed
* Closing connection 0
```

alex infra: I queried our DNS provider (AWS Route53) — no recent changes. TTLs normal.
cloudflare-support-bot: Automated note: Cloudflare observed degraded handshake success rates for a subset of edge POPs in US-West. Affected features: TLS termination and HTTP/2. Incident link: https://cloudflarestatus.example/INC-2026-0423-1
maria oncall: Great, that matches. Impact: non-trivial portion of us-west traffic failing; fallback to other edges inconsistent due to geolocation routing.
kia sre: Mitigation options: 1) Ask Cloudflare for immediate edge remediation / reroute. 2) Adjust routing to prefer alternate edges via R2/GEO steering (if supported). 3) Increase origin timeout/retry and surface graceful failures. 4) Bypass Cloudflare for critical customers (temporary LB change) — high risk.
sam support: We need quick customer-facing message, ETA unknown. Recommend StatusPage: Investigating with affected regions called out.
maria oncall: I’ll open an incident on statuspage. sam — please draft.
sam support: Draft: "We are investigating increased TLS handshake failures affecting API reachability for some users in US-West. Engineers are working with our CDN provider (Cloudflare)."
tyler eng-runtime: Also consider temporarily disabling HTTP/2 at Cloudflare for affected zone — sometimes HTTP/2 handshakes fail while HTTP/1.1 still succeeds. Can someone request that?
alex infra: I’m already opening a ticket with Cloudflare Support (priority: emergency) — ticket #CF-34219. Asking for immediate POP drain and TLS stack rollback for the region.
cloudflare-support-bot: Update: Cloudflare assigned to ticket CF-34219. Working on POP drain.
maria oncall: PagerDuty to backup oncall @kia sre. Handoff in 10.
kia sre: I’m on. Monitoring logs, running synthetic tests from multiple regions.
tyler eng-runtime: Running synthetic checks: us-west-1 fail, us-west-2 50% fail, us-east OK.
*** maria oncall updated incident priority to P1 ***
sam support: Support queue: 27 customer complaints in last 30m, some escalations flagged. Notifying account reps for top enterprise customers.
alex infra: Temporary mitigation attempt: routing TTL-based failover — increasing weight for nearest healthy edge is in progress. Will post when DNS propagation observed.
cloudflare-support-bot: CF update: POP drain started for IP range 104.16.96.0/20. Expected 5-10m to take effect.
maria oncall: Noting mitigation: Cloudflare POP drain in progress. Changing status to "Investigating — partial outage in US-West".
sam support: Status page updated. Support churn reduced slightly.
kia sre: Observability note: Some of our tracing shows sessions that retried succeed on second attempt — suggests client retry helps. Recommend increasing retry attempts and jitter in SDKs and gateway for next release.
tyler eng-runtime: Pushed a temporary rule on the gateway to increase client-side retries for 502/525 up to 3 with exponential backoff. Rolling out now.
alex infra: DNS failover changes showing partial routing to us-west backup edges. Latency slightly higher but lower failure rate.
cloudflare-support-bot: CF update: POP draining complete; TLS handshake success rates returning to baseline for drained POPs. Monitoring continues.
maria oncall: Seeing drop in handshake failures, error rate down from 18% to ~3% in US-West.
sam support: Support queue trending down, sending proactive note to top 10 affected customers.
IncidentBot: Reminder — document timeline and root cause steps in postmortem channel once stabilized.
maria oncall: Quick customer impact summary for PM/CS: "Intermittent TLS handshake failures affecting API reachability for a subset of US-West Cloudflare edges. Estimated impact window 2026-04-23T02:12Z to 2026-04-23T02:46Z, affecting ~12% of requests in that region. Primary mitigation: Cloudflare POP drain + DNS failover. No customer data exposure."
sam support: Sending to product and account teams now.
kia sre: Next steps: 1) Follow up with Cloudflare for RCA and RFC of their TLS change. 2) Add synthetic probes in additional regions and protocol families (HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2). 3) Update SDK retry guidance. 4) Postmortem in 24h.
alex infra: I'll request Cloudflare post-incident timeline and ask for permanent routing safeguards.
maria oncall: Handoff complete to kia sre. I’m off for now; monitor if escalation happens.
kia sre: Acknowledged. I’ll lead postmortem and coordinate with Cloudflare. Closing the active page once monitoring stable. :white_check_mark:
cloudflare-support-bot: Final update: CF incident resolved, ticket CF-34219 closed.
*** kia sre closed the alert at 1767564980 ***
